subject: physics
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: Which force keeps the planets in orbit around the Sun?
questions.explain: Gravity acts as the centripetal force that holds objects in their orbits around the Sun.

questions.q: Which type of object in the Solar System typically has a highly elliptical orbit?
questions.explain: Comets follow very elongated, highly elliptical orbits, whereas planets and moons have near-circular orbits.

questions.q: Stars begin their life cycle when gravity pulls together a cloud of dust and gas called a:
questions.explain: A star forms when gravity draws together the dust and gas of a nebula, causing it to heat up.

questions.q: During the main sequence stage, a star releases energy by fusing:
questions.explain: Main sequence stars fuse hydrogen nuclei into helium, releasing large amounts of energy.

questions.q: What is the final stage in the life cycle of a star with a mass similar to the Sun?
questions.explain: A Sun-sized star ends as a white dwarf after passing through the red giant stage and shedding its outer layers.

questions.q: The huge explosion that ends the life of a massive star is called a:
questions.explain: A massive star's core collapses and it explodes as a supernova, scattering material into space.

questions.q: Light from distant galaxies is red-shifted, meaning its observed wavelength is:
questions.explain: Red-shift means the light is shifted towards the red (longer wavelength) end of the spectrum as the source moves away.

questions.q: According to the Big Bang theory, the approximate age of the universe is:
questions.explain: The Big Bang model dates the origin of the universe to roughly 13.8 billion years ago.

questions.q: Which equation gives the orbital speed of a planet moving in a circular orbit of radius r and period T?
questions.explain: The planet travels the circumference (2πr) in one period T, so orbital speed equals distance divided by time.

questions.q: For a stable orbit, how does a planet's orbital speed change as its distance from the Sun increases?
questions.explain: Planets further from the Sun travel more slowly, so those closer in have greater orbital speeds.

questions.q: A planet moving in a circular orbit at constant speed still has a continually changing velocity because:
options: its direction of motion keeps changing
questions.explain: Velocity is a vector, so even at constant speed the changing direction of travel means the velocity is always changing.

questions.q: A main sequence star stays stable in size because:
options: the inward pull of gravity is balanced by the outward force from fusion
gravity is far stronger than the fusion force
no forces act on the star at all
questions.explain: Equilibrium between gravitational collapse and the outward pressure from fusion energy keeps the star stable.

questions.q: A star much more massive than the Sun may end its life as a:
questions.explain: After a supernova, a very massive star's core forms a neutron star, or a black hole if it is massive enough.

questions.q: The observation that more distant galaxies show greater red-shift is evidence that:
options: the Sun is at the centre of the universe
questions.explain: Greater red-shift for more distant galaxies shows they are moving away faster, indicating an expanding universe.

questions.q: The discovery of the cosmic microwave background (CMB) radiation is significant because it:
options: disproves the expansion of the universe
shows the universe is not expanding
questions.explain: The CMB is radiation left over from the early hot, dense universe and provides strong evidence for the Big Bang.

questions.q: Elements heavier than iron are mainly formed:
options: in a nebula before a star forms
questions.explain: Fusion in stars makes elements up to iron; the extreme conditions of a supernova create heavier elements and spread them into space.

questions.q: A planet orbits at a radius of 1.5 × 10¹¹ m with an orbital period of 3.15 × 10⁷ s. What is its approximate orbital speed?
Galaxy X shows a greater red-shift than Galaxy Y. This means Galaxy X is:
options: further away and moving away faster
closer and moving away more slowly
questions.explain: Greater red-shift indicates a faster recession speed, and more distant galaxies recede faster.

questions.q: Two moons orbit a planet. Moon A has a smaller orbital radius than Moon B. Compared with Moon B, Moon A has:
questions.explain: Objects in smaller orbits travel faster, so the closer moon has the greater orbital speed.

questions.q: Which sequence correctly shows the life cycle of a star with a similar mass to the Sun?
options: nebula → main sequence star → red giant → white dwarf
nebula → red giant → supernova → black hole
main sequence star → nebula → red supergiant → neutron star
red giant → nebula → white dwarf → supernova
questions.explain: A Sun-like star forms from a nebula, spends most of its life on the main sequence, swells into a red giant, then becomes a white dwarf.
